goldens.comment: The OptimizedCursorPaginator in organization_auditlogs.py attempts to use negative slice offsets on Django querysets, but Django querysets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError.
goldens.reasoning: C1 describes the same bug: negative offsets in Django queryset slicing raise an AssertionError.

goldens.comment: When requests are authenticated with API keys or org auth tokens (which have user_id=None), organization_context.member is None. Line 71 attempts to access organization_context.member.has_global_access without checking if member is None, causing an AttributeError crash when optimized_pagination=true is used, even though the request passed all permission checks with valid org:write scope.
goldens.reasoning: C2 flags the same missing null check on organization_context.member.has_global_access. It gives a different cause for member being None (superusers rather than API keys), but the underlying bug is the same.

goldens.comment: get_item_key assumes a numeric key, but the paginator is used with order_by=-datetime in the audit logs endpoint; calling math.floor/ceil on a datetime will raise a TypeError.
goldens.reasoning: C3 describes the same TypeError from calling math.floor/ceil on datetime keys.
None of the candidates mention importing a non-existent OptimizedCursorPaginator.

candidates: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result() passes negative offsets to Django queryset slicing which raises AssertionError since Django doesn't support negative indexing, despite comment claiming otherwise
organization_context.member.has_global_access is accessed without null check - superusers without org membership will have member=None causing AttributeError
OptimizedCursorPaginator used with order_by='-datetime' for audit logs will crash with TypeError because get_item_key uses math.floor/ceil on datetime values instead of numeric values
